final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position by conceding the same missing predicates identified in the initial report. That clarification matters to scope: the present record can support a limited statement that aggregate launch readiness passed and rehearsal severity was low. It does not support a policy-compliant certification finding, even with caveats, because the governing policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case, and the file still shows neither. Public guidance on documenting limitations and monitoring deployment supports good governance practice, but it does not override the internal policy condition. This remains suspicious rather than noncompliant because the record is incomplete, not because there is affirmative evidence that certification proceeded after the policy predicate was definitively rejected.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the municipal permitting assistant limitation was disclosed before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk-acceptance record covering this named launch use case limitation before launch.
The open legal ticket leaves the disclosure predicate unresolved at decision time.
The named city pilot commitments keep the gap materially relevant under the policy despite Product's non-core framing.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate release-policy predicate for a material limitation.
